summary: Consolidating several subsidiaries and achieving target budgets in a rising market

description:
Our overall strategy was to go-to-market early to identify compelling options for negotiation leverage, leveraging Thanos Realty’s reach and existing business relationships with the influencers and/or decision makers at the Landlords.  

We advised the client to consider timed short term lease extensions of several entities and locations, to align consolidation into two specific locations in order to avoid overlapping costs.

As part of our multi-prong approach, we also went-to-market early to mitigate rising market rents. During negotiations, we stressed how the Tenant’s prestigious brand would make it a good addition to the Landlord’s tenancy portfolio.

We also conducted workshops with each of the two competing Landlords on how they can be creative when it comes to improving key terms and value-add, to put them in a more favourable position when competing for the Tenant.

We negotiated a final 7% reduction in rent to fall within target budget for the new lease, along with a final 10% reduction in rent to fall within target renewal budget upon maturity of the new lease.

description:
Our project strategy was to deploy a crack team to first understand the Tenant’s expansion plans and assumptions over the next 10 years. This would ensure a future-proofed portfolio and clear negotiation parameters for a complex, 10-year plan.

Over the course of our efforts, we found that identifying a compelling relocation option was key to having the Renewal Landlord compete with creative solutions and value to retain the Tenant.

We engaged the Renewal Landlord on relocating existing tenancies to meet the Tenant’s expansion plans over contiguous floors. In doing so, lease expiry exposure the Renewal Landlord was facing was leveraged, to further drive their competitiveness.

The highly competitive renewal versus relocation engagement process led to the Renewal Landlord clearing existing tenancies to retain the Tenant over three exclusive, contiguous floors, inclusive of both generic and tailored building enhancements.  

Additionally, pre-agreed expansion options were successfully negotiated and secured for future-proofing the portfolio. This mitigated having to commit to potentially excessive space in advance.  

The highly competitive process also achieved a ~20% improvement in occupancy cost from the Renewal Landlord’s competitive position. And upon renewal, post-COVID 19 hybrid workplace strategy formulation and corresponding fit out project management would be conducted

title: Fast-growing financial institution
summary: Making a consolidation happen by striking a lower rent ahead of the market
description:
In order to meet the Tenant’s budget, we deployed the strategy to identify a Landlord who would lower rent expectations ahead of slowing down market. In return, secured occupancy would be a guarantee.

A consolidation of various entities and locations was preferred by the Tenant. However, a target cost needed to be achieved to make such a consolidation viable. To that end, we identified choice buildings with potential vacancies, and ones that were potentially more negotiable when it came to rent pricing.

We also leveraged the Tenant’s premium brand value they would bring to any building they occupied, while focusing on having the Landlord understand the viable costs involved for the Tenant. 

Concurrently, we worked with the Landlord to lower their rent expectations using data supporting an imminent office market slow down.

To close the deal, we successfully negotiated a final reduction in rent by 10%, leading the creation of a consolidation that would make a viable business case for the Tenant.
